Doctor of Philosophy in Geology
Location(s): Glassboro Campus
Return to: Programs of Study
The Ph.D. in Geology, housed with the School of Earth & Environment and College of Science and Mathematics, is a terminal degree program designed to prepare students for successful careers in academia or industry with an emphasis on research. The program offers a highly flexible curriculum with an emphasis on developing the skills, expertise, and commitment necessary for graduates to become leaders in the scientific research community.
The program is focused on training students to perform cutting-edge research activities that will foster scientific innovation and elevate the reputation of the University, and enhance the quality of educational offerings at all levels. The program is composed of core courses in geology, electives, research, and the production of a research-based dissertation. Students begin their research projects within the first year of the program and are largely focused on that research by their second year. Through our curriculum, students develop a robust foundation in geology and selected areas of interest through intensive and focused coursework, and will then build on and expand their theoretical and methodological expertise through the conduct of their research. The program offers the following major areas of specialty in paleontology, planetary science (cosmochemistry, asteroid science, and meteoritics), global climate interactions, and classic field-based geology research. The program of study includes training in the professional and soft skills necessary for a successful scientific career, including identification and pursuit of external funding, teaching, and outreach.
Ph.D. students have access to world-class research facilities, including specialized laboratories for the preparation and analysis of terrestrial and ocean sediments and rock samples for paleoceanographic investigation, cosmogenic nuclide dating, sedimentological analysis, and paleontology. The Jean and Ric Edelman Fossil Park, a unique living laboratory, offers opportunities for study in multiple subject matter areas within the geosciences and for inquiry into critical issues involving climate change, biodiversity, and sustainability. The Fossil Park’s state-of-the-art museum and visitor center is a forum for outreach to the community at large on these issues, as well as on STEM education that our students can utilize for their education and research.
Required Courses: 72 s.h.
GEOL 01701 - Seminar in Geology Credits: 4
GEOL 01702 - Avanced Seminar in Geology Credits: 4
GEOL 01703 - Proposal Writing and Grant Management in Geology Credits: 3
GEOL 01704 - Communication and Ethics in Geology Credits: 3
GEOL 01705 - Graduate Colloquium Credits: 2
GEOL 01706 - Advanced Graduate Colloquium Credits: 2
GEOL 01710 - Fundamental Research I Credits: 6
GEOL 01711 - Fundamental Research II Credits: 6
GEOL 01712 - Topics in Graduate Geology Credits: 3 (taken twice)
GEOL 01713 - Advanced Topics in Graduate Geology Credits: 3 (taken twice)
GEOL 01730 - Dissertation Research in Geology Credits: 1 to 12 (Total of 6 semesters of dissertation research required)
Total Required Credits for the Program: 72 s.h.
Foundation Courses
None
Graduation/Exit, Benchmark, and/or Thesis Requirements:
Students must successfully pass the Ph.D. qualification exam and candidacy exam.
Students must complete and defend a doctoral dissertation.
Minimum Required Grades and Cumulative GPA
The Doctor of Philosophy in Geology is a Category 1 program.
For details regarding satisfactory academic progress and graduation requirements, please visit Academic Program Policy Categories
